1004036.etyen:
First word past participle of koke (“cook, boil”), from Middle Low German kôken, kâken, from Old Saxon *kokōn, from Proto-West Germanic *kôken, from Latin cocō, coquō (“to cook”), from earlier *quoquō, from Proto-Italic *kʷekʷō (“to cook”), from Proto-Indo-European *pékʷeti (“to be cooking”), from *pekʷ- (“to cook”).
Last word from Old Norse egg n (“egg”), from Proto-Germanic *ajją (“egg”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ōwyóm (“egg”), likely from *h₂éwis (“bird”), possibly from *h₂ew- (“to enjoy, consume”).

1004804.etyen:
From dialectal Norwegian silung, with the first syllable apparently remodelled through association with svele (“small or half-grown salmon”) or a related dialectal form. The older form is represented by Norwegian Nynorsk silung (“small or half-grown salmon”), from Old Norse sílungr (“small salmon; trout”), itself derived from síl (“herring; probably originally fish fry”), from Proto-Germanic *sīlą.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk svelung, sveling, and Icelandic silungur (“small salmon; trout”).

1005060.etyen:
Unknown. Apparently belonging to the same expressive interjectional family as hoi (“exclamation of surprise, joy, or attention”) and hoie (“to holler, call out”), and perhaps an expanded form of hoi.
Compare older Danish hoja and German hoi (“hey; call”).
